topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: It frames the lecture topic, addresses the complexity of complement nomenclature, and outlines the scope of the class.

topics.label: Fundamentals and the Central Role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core overview of the cascade, its naming conventions, and the central biochemical role of C3 activation.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct upstream recognition pathways that generate convertases and trigger complement activation.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the primary downstream effector functions through which activated complement targets and eliminates pathogens.

topics.label: Regulation of Complement and Host Protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical Presentations of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic analyzes the specific disease presentations and infection susceptibilities caused by deficiencies in complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens adapt to counteract complement activation and how these evasion proteins are utilized clinically and experimentally.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
